observation.visible_scene: A near-black frame containing a tall, narrow orange-yellow flame anchored in the lower-left (base near x~285-290, y~350). Several small, fixed points of light sit in the otherwise empty background: a white dot upper-center (~425,205), a white dot far right (~895,235), and a tiny orange ember mid-frame (~485,290). A second, dimmer orange flame/ember appears around (590,270). The fixed background dots stay at identical pixel positions across all frames, indicating a stationary camera.
visible_changes: The main flame's tip rises slightly and its height stabilizes within the first ~0.2 s (tip y from ~290 to ~270), then remains roughly constant.

The main flame's orientation gradually shifts: the tip moves rightward relative to the base (tip x from ~272 leaning left to ~300-302 leaning right), so the flame sways/tilts from a left-leaning to a more upright/right-leaning posture while its base stays put.
The main flame's brightness and width flicker subtly frame to frame.
The secondary orange ember near (590,270), sometimes with a smaller dot just below it (~600,290), flickers on and off / fades in and out rather than translating.
The three background dots (two white, one orange) remain static throughout.
outside_clip_unknowns: The cause of the flame's sway/tilt (e.g., air draft) is not visible.
The identity of the flame source (match, lighter, candle) and of the distant light points is unknown.
Whether the flame motion continues or reverses beyond the cropped endpoints is not shown.
uncertain_details: The rightward drift of the flame tip could partly reflect internal flame wobble rather than a uniform lean; the base position is essentially fixed.
The secondary ember's changes are best described as flickering/appearing-disappearing; whether it also moves slightly is hard to confirm.
Camera motion is judged negligible because background reference points do not shift.
